title: dead-letter: turn .eml email exports into clean Markdown
one_liner: Convert .eml and .mbox email to clean Markdown with YAML front matter, locally, for LLM pipelines.
card_description: A local CLI, Python API and MCP server that turns raw MIME email into readable Markdown with YAML front matter, retained attachments and conversion diagnostics. No upload or API key.
demo_caption: 27-second demo of released dead-letter 0.4.10 on a synthetic inbox: raw MIME in, Markdown with YAML front matter out, a copy-only bundle with the decoded CSV, and diagnostics.
social_alt: dead-letter social card. Left: the hooded mail-carrier logo, the name dead-letter and the line "Email exports to clean, LLM-ready Markdown". Right: real output from dead-letter 0.4.10 on a synthetic order email, showing its raw MIME headers above the Markdown file with YAML front matter that the conversion produced.
demo_alt: Animated demo of dead-letter 0.4.10 converting a synthetic inbox in five scenes: raw MIME input, a CLI folder conversion, Markdown with YAML front matter, a copy-only Cabinet bundle with the decoded CSV attachment, and a report with diagnostics.
site_paragraph: dead-letter converts .eml and .mbox email exports into clean Markdown with YAML front matter. Threads are split, signatures stripped and attachments listed or kept as decoded files, so the text is ready for RAG, LLM pipelines or a Markdown knowledge base. It runs locally as a CLI, a Python API or an MCP server, with no account, upload or API key. The demo shows released version 0.4.10 on synthetic mail.
